subject: Dedicated reservation options — Aperture Health
messages:
From: Sally Warden <sally.warden@aperturehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aperture DevOps <devops@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation inquiry

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. The engineering and procurement teams asked me to gather concrete reservation/commitment options so we can budget and align with legal. High level goals: low-latency inference for our real-time triage product, predictable monthly spend, and the ability to scale quickly in Q4.

Could you send 2–3 proposal options that show:
- cluster size (GPU count and model lanes)
- minimum guaranteed GPUs per month (min floor)
- a 6-month ramp schedule with activation windows
- indicative unit economics (per-token or per-GPU-hour guidance)

Also looping in devops for any networking/region constraints. If you have a one-page worksheet they can plug numbers into, please attach.

Appreciate it — aim is to review internally next Wednesday.

—Sally
Sally Warden
Head of ML Platforms, Aperture Health
Sally Warden | Aperture Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sally Warden <sally.warden@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Aperture DevOps <devops@aperturehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation inquiry

Sally — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a lightweight worksheet (aperture-gpu-worksheet.xlsx) and a short proposal PDF that sketches three commitment tiers. High-level summary below; PDF has the lane mapping and cost assumptions.

Option A — Conservative (Pilot + safety buffer)\- Cluster size: 8 GPUs (2 serving lanes: 6 GPU low-latency lane, 2 GPU batch lane)\- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 6 GPU-equivalents/month\- Ramp: Month 1: 25% activation (1–2 GPUs live), Month 2: 50%, Month 3: 75%, Month 4–6: 100%\- Notes: Good for a 6–12 week pilot, lowest upfront commitment, supports burst to 8 GPUs for short windows.

Option B — Balanced (Growth-aligned)\- Cluster size: 24 GPUs (3 serving lanes: 12 GPU low-latency, 8 GPU mixed, 4 GPU batch)\- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 12 GPU-equivalents/month\- Ramp: Month 1: 40%, Month 2: 60%, Month 3: 80%, Month 4: 100%\- Notes: Predictable throughput for production traffic, recommended if Q4 growth target is +3–5x.

Option C — Anchored High-throughput\- Cluster size: 48 GPUs (4 serving lanes: 24 GPU low-latency, 12 GPU mixed, 8 GPU batch/embeddings)\- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 24 GPU-equivalents/month\- Ramp: Month 1: 50%, Month 2: 75%, Month 3: 90%, Month 4: 100%\- Notes: Lower per-unit cost via reserved capacity and tighter latency SLOs; includes warm-standby and cross-region failover option.

Unit economics in the PDF assume quantized model runtime on A100-equivalent hardware and include projected batching and KV cache savings; worksheet lets you toggle quantization levels and target p95 latency to see cost impact.

Next steps I propose: 1) Aperture fills the worksheet with expected Q3/Q4 token volumes, 2) we sync for a 30-minute sizing call (I can bring Marissa for pricing and Rishi for SLA/ops), 3) we iterate to a deal term.

I'll also note the legal team prefers to see a clear activation/fallback clause (can ramp down commitment in Month 4 with 60 days notice) — Marissa, recommend we include a sample clause in the PDF.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sally Warden <sally.warden@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aperture DevOps <devops@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation inquiry

Sally — adding two practical items from pricing and legal perspective:

1) Pricing bands: the PDF includes a monthly committed $/GPU-hour band and a transient burst rate. Example: committed band saves ~28% vs burst. We'll call out a blended expected monthly effective rate in the worksheet.

2) Activation windows and credits: for Options B and C we typically offer a 2-week warm-up credit (applies as service credit if activation is delayed past the agreed start). For Option A we can offer a pilot credit to offset first-month runbooks.

3) SLAs and penalty: Rishi, please confirm latency/availability targets we can commit to for the 24 GPU Balanced tier.

Sally — attached is the revised PDF (redwood-dedicated-options-03.pdf) with a sample contract paragraph for fallback/decommit and a simple table that maps traffic tier -> recommended lane split. Please review the worksheet and drop your expected Q3 token volumes; that will let us show a modeled monthly cost.

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Sally Warden <sally.warden@aperturehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aperture DevOps <devops@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation inquiry

Thanks Karthik/Marissa — this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers from our side:
- We'll populate the worksheet with conservative and aggressive Q3/Q4 projections by EOD Wednesday.
- Preferred region: us-west (devops note: prefer single-region start with cross-region failover later).
- For the initial legal review, can you surface the fallback/decommit language and the warm-up credit wording as a separate short excerpt? Legal wants to see just the few lines they need to approve.

Can we lock a 30-minute call Thursday 9:00am PT to walk through the worksheet? Invite sent.

Attachments: Aperture will attach a 1-pager of expected daily requests (devops@aperturehealth.com) to the calendar invite.

See you Thursday — Sally
